name: Esomeprazole
sections: White to slightly coloured crystalline powder (magnesium trihydrate).
The S-enantiomer of omeprazole, giving higher and more consistent plasma levels. First approval/introduction: Patented 1993; approved 2000 (EU), US FDA February 2001 (AstraZeneca).

S-isomer of omeprazole; irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase, providing more consistent acid suppression. Receptor / target profile: Irreversibly blocks H+/K+-ATPase in gastric parietal cells.
Summary: Bioavailability ~64% (single dose) rising to ~89% (repeated). Tmax 1–2 h. ~97% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19/3A4. Half-life 1–1.5 h.
Erosive reflux oesophagitis – healing and maintenance
Healing and prevention of NSAID-associated gastric ulcers
Erosive oesophagitis: 40 mg once daily for 4–8 weeks; maintenance 20 mg/day
H. pylori: 20 mg twice daily with amoxicillin and clarithromycin for 7–14 days
Take at least 1 h before a meal
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Clopidogrel – reduced antiplatelet effect; avoid combination
LOTUS (Galmiche et al., JAMA 2011) – esomeprazole as effective as laparoscopic anti-reflux surgery over 5 years.
Higher erosive oesophagitis healing rates than omeprazole in head-to-head trials.
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Do not use long-term without review
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
